heroHeadline: FDA Accepts Intellia's Lonvo-Z BLA with Priority Review — First In Vivo CRISPR Therapy on Track for 2027 Approval; Columbia Study Finds Base Editing in Human Embryos Efficient but Genomically Unpredictable
heroSubtitle: September 8, 2026: The FDA accepted Intellia Therapeutics' Biologics License Application for lonvoguran ziclumeran (lonvo-z) and granted Priority Review, with a PDUFA target action date of March 10, 2027 and no advisory committee currently planned. Backed by Phase 3 HAELO data showing an 87% reduction in hereditary angioedema attacks, lonvo-z is on track to become the world's first approved in vivo CRISPR-based therapy, with a potential US launch in H1 2027. September 9, 2026: Columbia University researchers Stepan Jerabek and Dieter Egli reported in Nature that base editing PCSK9 in human embryos before the first cell division achieved the intended edit in 100% of a resulting embryo's daughter cells, but also produced an array of additional, unpredictable genomic alterations — reigniting debate over the safety bar for any future clinical germline editing. Separately, a September 3, 2026 Lancet case report from Mass General Brigham described a patient who lived 271 days without dialysis on a CRISPR-Cas9-edited eGenesis pig kidney before receiving a human transplant, the longest dialysis-free xenotransplant survival reported to date.
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA, EMA, MHRA, NIH, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Science, NEJM, Cell), ClinicalTrials.gov, and major science outlets. Clinical data reflects published peer-reviewed results only.
